cyRAVEN

Flow cytometry files in, population frequencies, a UMAP and statistics out.

Every sample is gated separately, and the report is one file.

Quick start Get started

Quick start

You need Docker. Four commands, then open one file.

1. Get the image

docker pull bhagesh/cyraven:1.0.0
docker tag bhagesh/cyraven:1.0.0 \
  cyraven:1.0.0

2. Write the demo data: 35 FCS files, a sample sheet and a config.

docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/w" \
  cyraven:1.0.0 --demo /w/demo

3. Check the inputs. Takes seconds. It should end with no problems found.

docker run --rm \
  -v "$PWD/demo:/data:ro" \
  -v "$PWD/results:/results" \
  cyraven:1.0.0 \
  --dir /data/fcs \
  --samples /data/samples.csv \
  --config /data/panel.yaml \
  --group-column cohort \
  --reference-group "GvHD grade 1" \
  --outdir /results \
  --check

4. Run it. A few minutes.

docker run --rm \
  -v "$PWD/demo:/data:ro" \
  -v "$PWD/results:/results" \
  cyraven:1.0.0 \
  --dir /data/fcs \
  --samples /data/samples.csv \
  --config /data/panel.yaml \
  --group-column cohort \
  --reference-group "GvHD grade 1" \
  --outdir /results

5. Open results/report.html. Every figure and table is in that one file.

On Windows, run these in Git Bash or WSL with MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 in front of each command. In PowerShell, end each continued line with a backtick instead of \, and write ${PWD} for $PWD.

How it works 

FCS files · sample sheet · config
                ▼
        1  Read the files
                ▼
       2  Gate each sample
                ▼
      3  Score populations
                ▼
     4  Uncertainty and UMAP
                ▼
        5  Compare groups
                ▼
           report.html
  1. Read. Each file is opened and its channels are matched to markers. Acquisition stability over time is checked. → acquisition_qc.csv
  2. Gate each sample. Leukocytes, singlets, live cells and CD45+ cells are found first. Then each marker is cut at the lowest point between its negative and positive peaks, inside that sample. → thresholds_used.csv, gating_qc.png
  3. Score populations. Cells meeting each rule in your YAML are counted, for example CD3: above and CD4: above. → population_frequencies.csv
  4. Uncertainty and UMAP. Each cut is re-derived on resampled events to see how far it moves. A UMAP is built from an equal number of cells per sample. → threshold_uncertainty.csv, umap_overview.png
  5. Compare. Groups are tested with one value per sample. Populations are tested against clinical variables and followed across visits. → group_comparison_stats.csv, clinical_association.csv

If a marker shows no gap between negative and positive cells, step 2 uses a fixed percentile instead and labels the cut quantile_fallback. The population is still reported; check it before you use the number.

What it can do

Feature Flag
A gate placed inside each sample always on
Uncertainty for every cut and frequency on by default
Several smoothing levels and gate shapes --adaptive-gates
Skip a gate the data cannot support --auto-fix-gates
Tests between groups --group-column
Clinical scores and lab values --clinical-columns
Absolute cell numbers --total-counts
Every figure again per visit --split-by-timepoint
Batch check, and correction --batch-column, --correct-batch
Clustering, for unlisted populations --explore
FMO controls as gate references fmo_for column
FCS files with gate columns, for FlowJo --flowjo-export
Gating-ML 2.0 gate export --export-gates

Your own data

You write two files: a sample sheet (one row per FCS file) and a config (the populations to score). Start both from a template.

docker run --rm -v "$PWD/data:/data" \
  cyraven:1.0.0 \
  --dir /data/fcs --recursive \
  --write-samples /data/samples.csv
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/data:/data" \
  cyraven:1.0.0 \
  --write-template /data/analysis.yaml

Fill in the sheet’s patient_id and group columns, and edit the populations: section of the config. Run with --check until it reports no problems, then run without it. Get started explains both files and every option.

Before you use a number

  • Open gating_qc.png first. It draws each cut on the data it came from. A cut on the side of a peak, instead of in the gap, is visible there and in no table.
  • A quantile_fallback cut found no gap. Look at that population before you report it.
  • Frequencies are shares of CD45+ cells. One population’s share can rise because another fell, with no change in its cell number. Only --total-counts shows a change in size.
  • Tests use one value per sample, never single cells, so a longer acquisition does not inflate significance. With several samples per patient, pair them with --paired-column patient_id and --condition-column timepoint.

Why gate each sample separately

Manual gating varies between operators. When 38 operators gated the same files, the median expanded uncertainty was 3.6%, and experience made no significant difference (Grant et al., 2021, PDA J Pharm Sci Technol 75:33). Across 320 clinical samples analysed by six technologists, the remaining spread followed the operator more than the instrument (Mead et al., 2026, Cytometry B, doi:10.1002/cyto.b.70048).

Copying one set of gate coordinates to every sample does not fix this. Samples stain with different intensity, so a fixed cut suits some and not others. cyRAVEN places each cut inside its own sample and reports how precisely that cut is determined.

Without Docker

Docker pins R 4.4.3, a dated CRAN snapshot and Bioconductor 3.20. Newer package versions can move gates and UMAP coordinates slightly, so results may differ a little outside it.

install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("flowCore")
remotes::install_github("bhagesh-h/cyRAVEN")
library(cyRAVEN)
write_demo_cohort("demo")
run_cyraven(list(
  dir = "demo/fcs", outdir = "results",
  samples = "demo/samples.csv",
  config = "demo/panel.yaml",
  group_column = "cohort",
  reference_group = "GvHD grade 1"))

The chapters are not installed with the package, so browseVignettes() returns nothing; function help such as ?run_cyraven is installed.

Citation 

citation("cyRAVEN")

If you use the clustering, also cite FlowSOM (Van Gassen et al., 2015, Cytometry A 87:636). For the differential state tests, also cite diffcyt (Weber et al., 2019, Commun Biol 2:183).
